new_agent_audits.name: phf_generator
new_agent_audits.notes: Проверено агентом, не человеком. Full source read: Cargo.toml, Cargo.toml.orig, README.md, src/lib.rs, src/ptrhash.rs and src/bin/gen_hash_test.rs. Archive SHA-256 aeb62e0959d5a1bebc965f4d15d9e2b7cea002b6b0f5ba8cde6cc26738467100. Reviewed bounded slice/index operations, seed search, bucket placement/displacement, ptrhash pilot eviction/remapping, integer-width assumptions, fixed RNG seed and returned table permutation/lookup agreement. No unsafe, FFI, filesystem, network, subprocess or content logging in the generator; bundled benchmark binary only synthesizes in-memory strings. Deployed table correctness is included, not just safe execution of a build script. Important usage restriction: root uses immutable, modest-sized distinct build-time keys through phf_macros/phf_codegen/string_cache_codegen, not attacker-controlled runtime keys or custom hash callbacks. Read caller duplicate guards (phf_macros Map::from_parsed/check_duplicates; phf_codegen Map/OrderedMap::build) and string_cache_codegen BTreeSet insertion/filtering before generate_hash. Duplicate or permanently colliding custom inputs can loop indefinitely; no universal termination guarantee is claimed. Tables larger than u32 and hostile runtime generation are outside this reviewed root use; adding either requires renewed review. Synthetic tests check empty and varied distinct sets, full map permutations, actual phf_shared lookup, determinism, and codegen duplicate rejection; 4/4 debug and 4/4 release on Windows x86_64. ptrhash also read/tested although inactive in root. Dependencies, emitted Rust syntax in external code generators and unrelated clients remain separate. ADR 0102 batch 5; file hashes/caller sections, active feature evidence and limitations in review-2026-11-26-batch-5.json.
